_readme: Paraphrase battery for src/surgvu/router.py.
The router was designed against exactly 11 questions -- the public Cat-2
sample at /staging/groups/bhaskar_opscribe/surgvu/cat2_sample. Those are
last year's TEST questions, so they are distributionally representative,
but 11 items cannot show how a rule behaves on a phrasing nobody wrote
down. This file is that missing distribution, written by hand.
Every variant is labelled with the intent the router SHOULD pick, not the
intent it currently picks. Variants that were expected to fail at the time
of writing are marked with an `expected_to_fail_at_authoring` note; they
are the point of the exercise, not an accident.
Fields:
question   the paraphrase
source     which of the 11 sample questions it paraphrases, or 'novel'
family     grouping label, for reading the report
intent     the INTENT_* constant it should route to
classes    (optional) the taxonomy classes mentioned_tool_classes should
resolve out of the question -- a finer check than intent,
because a presence question can route correctly and still
test the wrong tool
scenario   (optional) key into `scenarios`; with `answer`, asserts the
end-to-end string. Used for the polarity traps and the
low-confidence policy, where the intent is right and the
ANSWER is the thing at risk.
answer     (optional) the exact string answer_question should return
note       why this variant exists

driver_and_cadiere._note: case122/125-like: a needle driver and a cadiere forceps, suturing.

no_driver_cutting._note: case123/124-like: scissors, bipolar and a retractor; no driver.

case129_low_confidence._note: case129 verbatim from outputs/perception_sample.json: every tool fell below its tuned threshold, so tools_present is empty while three probabilities are still over one half.

nothing_at_all._note: Every probability zero and an empty presence list: no evidence of any kind.

variants.question: Is a forceps being used here?
variants.note: singular subject

variants.question: Are forceps present in this clip?
variants.note: the word 'clip' must stay a video clip

variants.question: Does the surgeon use forceps?
variants.note: agentive rephrasing

variants.question: Did the team use any forceps?
Are any forceps visible in the video?
Were any forceps installed on the arms?
Is there no forceps in use here?
variants.note: TRAP: a cadiere IS present, so 'is there no forceps' is answered No. Intent is already right; the answer must flip.

variants.question: Are there no forceps being used?
variants.note: TRAP: a bipolar forceps IS present, so 'are there no forceps' is answered No even though the question is negative. See the sibling below for the other polarity.

variants.question: Are there no needle drivers in this clip?
variants.note: TRAP: no driver present, so 'are there no drivers' is Yes.

variants.question: Aren't forceps being used here?
variants.note: TRAP-INSIDE-A-TRAP: 'Aren't X used?' is NOT existential negation. English answers it Yes when X is used. Contracted openers must be polar but must not flip.

Is a ProGrasp being used?
variants.note: commercial name without the class head-noun

variants.question: Is a Maryland bipolar in use?
variants.note: 'Maryland Bipolar Forceps' minus its head noun; 'maryland' is unique to one class in config/commercial_names.json

Is a needle holder involved?
Is a needle driver not involved in this procedure?

variants.question: Is the needle driver part of the instrument set?

Needle driver - is one being used?
variants.note: TRAP: topicalised tool, polar opener in the second clause.

variants.question: What procedure does this summary describe?

variants.note: BY DESIGN: a polar question about the procedure wants 'Yes', not the name of the procedure, so unknown_polar is the correct route.

variants.question: Isn't tissue being cut during this clip?
Is tissue being coagulated?
variants.note: BY DESIGN: coagulation is not division. There is no cauterisation intent, and the polar fallback is the honest answer.

variants.question: Are the scissors cutting tissue?
variants.note: AMBIGUOUS ON PURPOSE: names a tool AND asks about cutting. The presence rule currently wins. Both routes give the same answer for scissors, so this is a labelling disagreement, not a scoring loss.
